title: How dark should the selected line be
reference_disclaimer: Light palette only, offscreen, device pixel ratio 1.0. All four builds are commit 46fa6ce with one colour literal changed. Zoomed images are nearest-neighbour 2x crops, so soft edges are magnification and not rendering. These captures are re-rendered since you last looked: the change-group boundary is now a neutral grey rule on the edge above the group (BPR-0202), so nothing blue competes with the selection any more. The selected line in every capture is 'teardown_render_pipeline(handle);' - the line directly below the grey rule, and the first line of the red removed block. The earlier batch is withdrawn: its crops were cut from the wrong part of the window and showed you chrome instead of diff.

subjects.display_name: Selection shade A - the smallest step that is still a change
subjects.description: The selected line is 'teardown_render_pipeline(handle);' - directly below the grey boundary rule, and the first line of the red removed block. In the current build it is washed grey-lilac at a strength you already told me was too light. This candidate darkens the selection colour from #D8E9FF to #A8CCF0, keeping the same 28% translucency so the red removed tint still shows through. Compare against the four-panel strip: top panel is the current build, this candidate is the second.
acceptance_criteria: You can tell which line is selected without being told
The red removed tint is still readable through the selection
It does not read as a solid block that hides the code
known_concerns: Measures dE76 8.9 against the removed band it sits on, below the ~10 that counts as comfortably distinct - this is the weakest of the three candidates and may still be too subtle
Only the Light palette is covered; the other three shipped palettes need the same decision

Light palette only. The dark scheme cannot be captured until BPR-0201 is resolved: the app reported a dark profile applied while rendering light pixels, so a dark capture is not yet evidence of anything.

audit_verdict.note: dE76 8.9 against the band underneath, short of the 10 threshold. Included because 'a little darker' was your direction and this is the most conservative reading of it.

subjects.display_name: Selection shade B - clears the distinctness threshold
subjects.description: Same as candidate A but darker again, #8FBCEA at the same 28% translucency. This is the lightest of the three that clears the distinctness threshold. In the four-panel strip it is the third panel down.
acceptance_criteria: You can tell which line is selected without being told
The red removed tint is still readable through the selection
It does not read as a solid block that hides the code
known_concerns: Only the Light palette is covered; the other three shipped palettes need the same decision

Still fails the WCAG 3:1 non-text luminance minimum, which no colour can reach at 28% opacity. I am no longer treating that threshold as the target for a background wash - it is the wrong measure for a tint and hitting it would swamp the syntax colouring. If you want that requirement honoured literally, the alpha has to go and the band becomes opaque.

Light palette only. The dark scheme cannot be captured until BPR-0201 is resolved: the app reported a dark profile applied while rendering light pixels, so a dark capture is not yet evidence of anything.

audit_verdict.note: dE76 11.2 against the band underneath, clear of the 10 threshold, with the underlying tint still visible.
